baslik: The Day a Mountain Blew Its Own Side Off

sahneler.metin: This mountain lost thirteen hundred feet of its summit in seconds.
May eighteenth, 1980. Mount St. Helens, Washington State.
A strong earthquake shakes loose the entire north face of the volcano.
It becomes the largest landslide ever recorded on Earth.
That uncorks the magma inside like a shaken bottle.
A sideways blast flattens whole forests twenty miles away.
Ash climbs fifteen miles into the sky and circles the globe.
Fifty seven people never make it out.
A mountain can rebuild itself, and this one still is.
